subject: SLA & streaming UX tradeoffs — discovery recap and next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: SLA & streaming UX tradeoffs — discovery recap and next steps

Alicia — great to meet today. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks.

High-level pain points you flagged
- Tail latency spikes during merchant-activity peaks (even with identical model/config).
- First-byte delay for streaming-based recommendations hurts perceived responsiveness in the product.
- Large variance between steady-state throughput and short bursts (peaks up to ~700 concurrent streams).

Current stack (what you said)
- Recommendation service on GCP using Triton serving; model is a quantized Llama-2-13B variant.
- Autoscaling based on pods but slow warm-up for model KV caches after scale events.
- Observability: Datadog traces + aggregated per-request logs (you offered a sample log).

Success criteria you gave (confirm if I captured correctly)
- p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 200ms under peak concurrency (goal).
- First-byte streaming latency under 400ms for interactive sessions.
- Stable throughput that sustains 40k tokens/sec during 10–15m bursts without error-rate increases.

What we think (short)
- Tail spikes sound like cold KV cache + model warm-up behavior; streaming first-byte issues often trace to batching windows + initial token scheduling.
- We can trial a small dedicated Redwood footprint to validate prefix/KV cache warmers and tune batching to meet the first-byte SLO without sacrificing throughput economics.

Attachments: I attached a short trial plan and a draft SLA template to get aligned (redwood-trial-plan.pdf, SLA-template-v1.docx).

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive with engineering — 60 minutes (Marcus + Neha): proposed Tue 2026-05-26 or Wed 2026-05-27.
2) You share the sample service-profile log + one representative request trace (we can ingest into our test harness).
3) We spin a 2-week trial with a dedicated cluster (trial plan attached) and run a synthetic workload that mirrors your peak bursts.
4) After the trial, review p95 and streaming-first-byte metrics and decide rollout vs. further tuning.

If that aligns, I’ll confirm the calendar invite and add a lightweight test-spec doc to the Drive link.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim

Subject: Re: SLA & streaming UX tradeoffs — discovery recap and next steps

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the write-up. Quick confirmations and a few numbers from our side so you have concrete targets.

Confirming pain details
- Peaks: baseline concurrent streams ~120–180, daily peak up to ~700 for ~8–12 minutes (ad events window).
- Typical request size: 20–80 tokens per initial prompt, streaming response average 120 tokens for a recommendation card.
- Observed: p95 currently ~470ms during normal periods, spikes >1.2s during peak warmups. First-byte median ~420ms, first-byte tail hurts UX.

Targets (we’d be happy if)
- p95 <= 175ms across 90% of peak days; hard requirement is <= 250ms.
- First-byte <= 350–400ms.

Stack clarifications
- Yes, Triton on GCP (A100 right now). We use model quantization to 4-bit for cost.
- We can export sample traces/logs — attaching a short service profile for the 05/20 peak (finlytics-service-profile-05212026.log).

Budget constraints: we have a constrained POC budget; prefer to start with a small dedicated footprint — if the numbers look good we can expand.

Agree to the tech deep-dive — Tue 2026-05-26 works for Samir and me. Please include any pre-read so engineering can review before the call.

Alicia
Alicia Moreno
Head of Product — Realtime Recommendations | Finlytics

Subject: Re: SLA & streaming UX tradeoffs — discovery recap and next steps

Alicia — thanks for the numbers, that’s very helpful. A few notes from a technical POV and a lean test approach we’d propose.

Quick technical hypotheses
- Cold KV cache + model shard warmups are likely causing the >1s spikes after autoscale events.
- Batch windowing and initial-token prioritization impact first-byte; tiny non-zero batching windows can reduce overall CPU/GPU contention but increase first-byte for thin requests.

Lean trial footprint (what we can stand up quickly)
- Dedicated trial cluster: 1x 8-GPU A10 pool (or 2x A10 smaller nodes) with warmed KV cache preloading.
- Model variants: serve your quantized Llama-2-13B plus a trimmed 7B candidate to compare tail behavior.
- Workload: replay 3 representative traces (steady, 12-min burst, 30s micro-burst) you provided; run each 3x.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95 token latency, first-byte streaming latency, error-rate, GPU utilization, and memory swap events.

Instrumentation/hooks we need from you
- Sample request headers and path used to recreate your request routing.
- A flattened trace for one burst period (you attached the log — thanks).

Small optimization experiments in scope for trial
- KV-cache warmers (pre-warm on scale events).
- Lightweight prefix caching for repeated prompt patterns.
- Adaptive batching windows with first-byte priority for low-token requests.

If the trial meets your p95/first-byte targets we’ll produce a short runbook for rollout and a cost estimate for steady-state vs. Dedicated capacity.

Marcus Lin

Action items I’ll own this week
- Upload a short pre-read to the Drive link (test-spec + simple perf dashboard) by EOD tomorrow.
- Confirm trial cluster sizing and send the trial access keys for your engineering team.

Action items for Finlytics
- Please upload the sample traces you referenced (you attached one — perfect) and confirm a single representative API path we should replay.
- Confirm any security/allowlist needs for the trial cluster (IP ranges / service accounts).

Proposed success thresholds for judging the trial (please flag if we should change)
- p95 <= 200ms for the combination of steady + burst profiles (goal 175ms).
- First-byte median <= 350ms, tail (95th) <= 400ms.
- No increase in 5xx or client errors during peaks; graceful degradation path for best-effort scenarios.

If these read correctly, I’ll loop in our trials ops engineer and send the invite.

Best — Rachel
